First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{10}$ into the above, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{10}) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{10})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5})} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5})}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{5})\end{aligned}
$$
